sources.title: Dewei Wang, STAT 720 Time Series Analysis course notes
sources.locator: Full-text PDF pp. 29–31 (Section 2.2, Example 2.9, Lemma 2.2, Proposition 2.2, Theorem 2.4); pp. 34–38 (Sections 2.3.2–2.4, Theorem 2.5, Proposition 2.4, Theorem 2.6); pp. 51–55 (Sections 3.1–3.2, Remarks 3.1 and 3.3–3.4, Theorems 3.1–3.2); p. 65 (Theorem 4.4); pp. 90–92 (Section 6.1, Theorem 6.1 and Remarks 6.1–6.3).

contents.name: Example 2.9: an absolutely summable linear-process series converges in mean square
Lemma 2.2: mean and double-sum autocovariance formula for an absolutely summable linear process
Proposition 2.2: an absolutely summable two-sided filter preserves stationarity and transforms the autocovariance
Theorem 2.4: the Riesz–Fisher Cauchy criterion for mean-square convergence
contents.reason: The local filter proof constructs the almost-sure sum by Tonelli and bounds its L² tails directly, so this separate completeness criterion is not a premise.

contents.name: Theorem 2.5: existence of a stationary AR(p) solution iff its AR roots avoid the unit circle
contents.reason: The theorem assumes a Markovian innovation condition and makes a general existence claim; this batch assumes a weakly stationary solution and does not rely on that separate existence result.

contents.name: Theorem 2.5: causal AR(p) representation iff every AR root is outside the closed unit disk
Proposition 2.4: MA(1) noninvertibility boundary at a root in the closed unit disk
Theorem 2.6: printed MA(q) noninvertibility root condition
contents.reason: The printed statement says noninvertibility is equivalent to every root lying in the closed unit disk; this fails for mixed inside/outside roots. The assigned proof establishes the correct no-zero-in-the-disk equivalence by coefficient comparison.

contents.name: Section 3.1 ARMA definition and Remark 3.1 cancellation of common polynomial factors
Theorem 3.1: causal ARMA representation iff the autoregressive polynomial has no zero in the closed unit disk
Remark 3.3: a unit-circle autoregressive root precludes a stationary ARMA solution
contents.reason: The assigned B example proves the AR(1) case in full; no general ARMA nonexistence result is needed for the spectral theorem or claimed by the pair.

contents.name: Theorem 3.2: correct invertibility criterion; its printed converse proof compares coefficients through q although phi has degree p. The local proof removes the p/q typo and compares all coefficients.
Remark 3.4: causal and invertible representations when both root conditions hold
Theorem 4.4: spectral density for a stationary ARMA process without causal or invertible assumptions
Section 6.1 Yule–Walker equations and estimator
contents.reason: Yule–Walker is a different estimator from the fixed-order regression OLS theorem in this batch, so its equations are not used to justify the OLS limit.

contents.name: Theorem 6.1: asymptotic normality and variance consistency of the Yule–Walker estimator
contents.reason: The Yule–Walker asymptotic theorem concerns a moment estimator, not the conditional-martingale OLS estimator proved here; the two limits are not interchangeable.

contents.name: Remarks 6.1–6.3: Yule–Walker model fit, efficiency comparison, and approximate confidence intervals
contents.reason: These remarks concern a separate estimator and do not establish the fixed-order OLS covariance, residual mean-square consistency, or Wald limit claimed in this batch.

contents.name: Theorem 1: stationary Markovian AR(p) root criterion, one-sided representation, and exponential coefficient decay
Theorem 1: existence of a stationary Markovian AR(p) solution

contents.name: Theorem 2: dimension and root-form basis of homogeneous AR difference-equation solutions
contents.reason: This deterministic impulse-response result is not a premise for the assigned ARMA root, density, or inference statements.

contents.name: Theorem 3: MA(q) invertibility iff its polynomial has no zero in the closed unit disk
Section 2.5: ARMA recursion, common-zero cancellation, and causal/invertible transfer series
Section 2.6: autocovariance formula from a causal linear-process representation
Section 2.8.1: fixed-order AR least-squares estimator and lag-regression form
Section 2.8.1: Yule–Walker estimator and its large-sample comparison with least squares
contents.reason: The local OLS theorem proves a separate martingale limit under iid innovations independent of the past; the notes’ Yule–Walker comparison is not used as an OLS asymptotic proof.

contents.name: Section 2.8.2: AIC/BIC order selection and residual diagnostics
contents.reason: The assigned OLS result is explicitly fixed order and makes no data-selected order or residual adequacy claim.

contents.name: ARIMA extension on PDF pp. 35–36
contents.reason: The page covers stationary ARMA roots and spectra; differenced nonstationary ARIMA models are not needed for any assigned claim.
